newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pharma stocks end mixed on ratings, BUX edges up.
newsitem.headline: Pharma stocks end mixed on ratings, BUX edges up.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed on Tuesday as many investors were seen taking their time to digest 1996 earnings reports, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,613.89 points, up 27.20.

"The market is in a wait-and-see attitude," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities. "Despite the fact that all corporate results are out on the market, one cannot see a clear trend," he said. "Results need some time to be digested."
The last two corporate results, those of agricultural trading company Agrimpex and of Tesco 's Global, were published this morning.
Pharmaceuticals closed mixed after recommendations were made on them.
Richter closed at 12,600 forints, up 110, after ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett rated as 'buy.'
"Overall, (Richter's) results were very much in line with our expectations," Tommy Erdei, ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett's Budapest-based analyst said in a company update.
The other pharmaceuticals company, Egis closed unchanged at 11,050 forints after Hungarian securities house MEB rated it as 'buy.'

"We recommend Egis shares to buy because we regard them undervalued at thier current price (of 11,050 forints at Monday's close) compared to both its competitors and to its own performance," analyst Zoltan Kurali said in a company research.
Hotel firm Danubius closed lower amid heavy profit-taking, traders said. Danubius ended at 5,600 forints, down 350.
Oil company MOL drifted lower to close at 3,140 forints, down 30 as uncertainties over its privatisation remained.
"As far as MOL is concerned, buyers are definitely in a wait-and-see stance," Nagy said.
The planned new phase of MOL's privatisation keeps the market on its toes as it awaits details of its timing, pricing and offer size.
